PER-FRAME GENERATION (ADR 0017, amended — the strip-and-slice strategy was retired after two CI iterations cut subjects across cells): each frames[i] is a NON-EMPTY pose clause and becomes ONE dedicated FLUX image (opening + prompt + clause + style) under the layer's single pinned seed, so the whole subject appears in every image and only the described delta moves. nearForeground.$comment: Near-foreground parallax props (ADR-0047), repositioned for the single-wide street-wide.png décor (ADR-0057) per docs/game-design/spec-belliard-street-wide-repositioning.md §2 (13 props, gate lead-game-designer PASS 2026-07-21). factor is NEGATIVE (scrolls opposite/faster than the camera); clamped to [-0.5,-0.1] in getNearForeground. x is a full-street normalized anchor (0=left,1=right). trafficLight (x=0.388, on the passage) is the ONLY prop exempt from the maxH clamp (TRAFFIC_LIGHT_H_FRAC, NearForeground.tsx) and thus the only one that can rise into the window band — deliberately placed over the passage exclusion zone so its mast never sweeps an active pop window; the other props are clamped to maxH so non-occlusion holds by construction regardless of x. 2026-07-25 amendment (Bertrand-directed, "on ne voit plus le panneau Paris", then "ne garde qu'un seul panneau, celui de droite"): the §2.4 table left belliard with a SINGLE streetSign (x=0.46) and NearForeground.tsx halves each row on mobile by dropping every ODD entry of that row's list ORDER — that lone sign sat at near-row index 3 (odd), so belliard showed ZERO panneau PARIS on any mobile UA (verified in-browser). A first pass added two more signs (0.66, 0.885); Bertrand ruled three panneaux too many and kept only the RIGHTMOST, so the 0.46 and 0.66 signs are gone and the prop count is back to 13. The surviving streetSign x=0.885 is listed BEFORE the lamppost x=0.8 (x order DELIBERATELY broken there, and only there) so it takes near-row index 6 — EVEN, hence drawn on mobile; in x order it would fall on near-row index 7 (odd) and vanish again, reintroducing the exact original bug. The lamppost x=0.495 is back in plain x order (it had only been swapped to hand the now-deleted 0.46 sign an even index). ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING in this array: the mobile filter reads list order, not x. 2026-07-26 amendment (Bertrand-directed, "sur mobile on voit pas le lampadaire"): plain x order put BOTH lampposts (x=0.495, x=0.8) on odd near-row indices, so neither survived mobile — the streetSign fix above only ever guarded the sign. The lamppost x=0.495 is now listed BEFORE the bench x=0.6 (x order broken there, mirroring the streetSign trick) to take the EVEN index; that bench drops on mobile instead (the other bench, x=0.16, still shows). The x=0.8 lamppost is unchanged and still drops — one surviving lamppost is the fix, same bar as the streetSign. Drawn near row is now x=[0.16,0.34,0.388,0.6,0.495,0.72,0.885,0.8] on desktop and x=[0.16,0.388,0.495,0.885] on mobile; the sign's nearest same-row neighbour is 0.8 (clearance 0.085 ≥ 0.06) on desktop and 0.495 (clearance 0.39) on mobile. These invariants (a mobile-surviving sign + lamppost, ≥0.06 same-row x clearance on the row actually drawn in each mode) are pinned by src/game/levels/__tests__/nearForegroundDensity.test.ts — re-run it before reordering or inserting props.

windows.$comment: Single-wide décor (ADR-0057): 3 rows recalibrated on street-wide.png's real openings, per docs/game-design/spec-belliard-street-wide-repositioning.md §1 (gate lead-game-designer PASS 2026-07-21) — A lucarnes (mansard dormers) y=0.24, B étage noble (balcony doors) y=0.35, C persiennes (shuttered windows, densest) y=0.47. x/y normalized over the WHOLE single image (not per-tile as before). Exclusion zones respected column-by-column: passage 0.372-0.408, couture (mitoyen seam) 0.485-0.502, recess 0.595-0.610 (a second, undocumented building-seam/recessed-gable column found by direct pixel inspection of street-wide.png during the enemy-recalibration pass — a narrow near-solid dark vertical band measured consistently ~lum<52 across y=0.20-0.51 at x≈0.597-0.608, the mirror-image counterpart of the `passage` seam; this was the exact cause of a cop rendering on bare roof next to a chimney with no grille, since the old row-A x=0.62 landed inside it), pignon (blind gable) 0.788-0.812, edges <0.035/>0.965. 2026-07-21 targeted fix (6/54 zones, verified per-zone against real street-wide.png pixels, not re-derived wholesale): row A xs[7] 0.62→0.643 (was inside the new `recess` zone, no dormer there — real dormer sits at 0.643), xs[9] 0.835→0.847 (was on a chimney stack, real dormer at 0.847), xs[11] 0.95→0.96 (was mostly off the roof skylight, nudged onto it); row C xs[6] 0.257→0.238 (was in the gap between two real windows), xs[18] 0.746→0.753 (was half on the wall beside the window), xs[22] 0.928→0.947 (was in the gap between two real windows). All other x/y values verified already correct against the real image and left untouched.

levels.$comment: Niveau Final — l'Éden (ancien dancing), the boss-QTE venue (ADR-0053, story-boss-niveau-final-live). Single-facade mode (default, no `backdrop` field), same as stalingrad/vitry. INTERIOR venue: unlike the street levels this facade is a static hall interior held behind the whole boss tableau, so the exterior `sky`/`street` layers are DELIBERATELY DROPPED from `prompts` below (lead-art PROMPT GATE family PASS, 2026-07-20 — 'layer set with sky/street DROPPED for the interior') — the facade alone fills the frame ceiling-to-floor, which is exactly what satisfies the 'no dead sky-gap behind the boss {0,-5}' composition constraint. `gen-level-art.mjs` skips a layer cleanly when a level's `prompts` doesn't declare it, rather than sending FLUX a broken 'undefined' prompt (no hardcoded sky/street text ever reaches the generator for this level). `foreground`/`facade` prompt strings are copied VERBATIM from the gated draft `docs/art-direction/prompt-drafts/niveau-final-eden.md` (lead-art FAMILY PASS — Maud/concept-artist owns the prompt strings, this block's structure/ids/paths/sizes/windowGrid is dev-tooling-assets'). `size` uses the shared global `sizes.facade`/`sizes.foreground` (1280x768), no per-level override needed. A separate optional `ceiling` layer was drafted (bare-hook plaster detail) but is NOT included here per the draft's own default ('by default this layer drops' — the facade already carries the ceiling/cornice register); add it only if a future structural need requires a dedicated upper slot. Path `assets/levels/niveau-final/facade.png` (narrative wiring flag B, ADR-0023) generated via the existing `gen-level-art.mjs` → CI pipeline (ADR-0010), same as every other level — no new script/workflow needed for the backdrop itself.

windowGrid.$comment: cols RETUNED 5→4 (Bertrand escalation decision + lead-game-designer express DESIGN GATE PASS, 2026-07-21, docs/handoffs/story-boss-niveau-final-live.md — supersedes the original gated [E3] count of 5). The batch-2 l'Éden facade generated a 3-wall perspective room whose back wall carries 4 clear evenly-spaced frontal arches (not the gated 5 — a recurring generation drift, not a config bug); Bertrand accepted the art at 4 and ordered the grid retuned to match rather than a third reroll (the 2-batch cap was spent). Karim's gate confirmed the [E3] INTENT (even spacing + occupiable window-cop slots + [E5] merge-risk mitigation) is preserved at 4, and that [E5] risk actually IMPROVES (wider piers between fewer arches). rows=1 (a single row of arches, not multi-floor like the street levels) — computeWindowSlots/getWindowZones both special-case rows===1 to ny=0.5, so top/bottom are set equal and are inert by construction, kept for readability/consistency with the other per-level windowGrid blocks. NOTE (flagged, not fixed here — out of dev-tooling-assets' structural lane): the `facade` prompt string below still reads 'exactly 5 tall arched windows' — a residual mismatch against the now-4-pinned grid and the already-accepted 4-arch art; if `facade.png` is ever deleted and regenerated, the stale '5' text would reroll toward the wrong count again. Prompt-string content is concept-artist's (Maud's) lane, not touched here; routed to lead-art/concept-artist for a conscious amendment.
